segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the day of Pentecost arrived, they were all together in one place.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And suddenly there came from heaven a sound like a violent wind rushing in, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And tongues as of fire appeared to them, dividing among them, and one settled on each of them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit enabled them to speak out.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now there were Jews living in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At this sound the crowd came together and was thrown into confusion, because each one heard them speaking in his own language.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were astonished and marveled, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, aren’t all these who are speaking Galileans?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And how is it that each of us hears them in our own language, the one we were born into?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those who live in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya near Cyrene, and visitors from Rome,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: both Jews and converts, Cretans and Arabs—we hear them speaking in our own tongues about the great deeds of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were all astonished and at a loss, saying to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What does this mean?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But others mocked and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “They are full of sweet wine.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Peter, standing with the eleven, raised his voice and spoke out to them:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Fellow Jews and all you who live in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and give ear to my words.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For these people are not drunk, as you suppose; it is only the third hour of the day.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: No, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: ‘And in the last days it will be, God says, that I will pour out my Spirit on all humanity, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, and your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Even on my slaves, both men and women, I will pour out my Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And I will give wonders in the sky above and signs on the earth below: blood and fire and billowing smoke.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the day of the Lord comes, the great and splendid day.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Fellow Israelites, hear these words: Jesus the Nazarene, a man attested to you by God with deeds of power and wonders and signs that God did through him among you, as you yourselves know—

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: this man, handed over by the settled plan and foreknowledge of God, you nailed up by the hand of men outside the Law and killed.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But God raised him up, releasing him from the pangs of death, because it was not possible for him to be held by it.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For David says about him: ‘I saw the Lord always before me, for he is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Therefore my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced; and more, my flesh also will dwell in hope,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: because you will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor will you let your holy one see decay.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: You have made known to me the paths of life; you will fill me with gladness in your presence.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Brothers, I can speak to you frankly about the patriarch David: he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So, being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn to him with an oath to seat one of his descendants on his throne,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: he foresaw and spoke about the resurrection of the Messiah: that he was not abandoned to Hades, nor did his flesh see decay.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: This Jesus God raised up, and of that we are all witnesses.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Exalted, then, to the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this that you see and hear.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself says: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So let the whole house of Israel know for certain that God has made him both Lord and Messiah—this Jesus whom you crucified.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they heard this, they were pierced to the heart and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Brothers, what should we do?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Turn back, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For the promise is for you and for your children and for all who are far away, as many as the Lord our God calls to himself.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With many other words he bore solemn witness and kept urging them, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Be saved from this crooked generation.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand people were added that day.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the common life, to the breaking of bread and to the prayers.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Awe came over everyone, and many wonders and signs were taking place through the apostles.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All who believed were together and had everything in common.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were selling their property and possessions and distributing the proceeds to all, according to what each one needed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Day by day they devoted themselves to meeting with one mind in the temple; and breaking bread in their homes, they shared their food with rejoicing and simplicity of heart,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: praising God and having favor with all the people. And day by day the Lord added to their number those who were being saved.

notes.note: The Greek name means 'fiftieth'. It is the Jewish Feast of Weeks, a harvest festival held fifty days after Passover (Leviticus 23:15-16). As one of the pilgrimage festivals it brought Jews from abroad to Jerusalem, which explains the crowd in verses 5-11.

The Greek word means both the organ of speech and a language, as English 'tongue' still can ('mother tongue'). Here it means real foreign languages, as verses 6-11 make clear. 'Tongues' is kept so that the link with the 'tongues as of fire' in verse 3 stays visible.

A proselyte was a non-Jew who had fully converted to Judaism, which for men included circumcision. 'Proselytes' is the traditional rendering and is still used in formal translations; 'converts' says the same thing in current English.

The Greek address is literally 'Men, Jews'. Many translations render it 'Men of Judea', taking the word geographically alongside 'all you who live in Jerusalem'. It can equally be the ordinary term for the Jewish people, as in verse 5, and it is taken that way here; 'Fellow' reflects that Peter belongs to the group he addresses.

notes.phrase: the third hour of the day
notes.traditional: the third hour of the day
notes.note: Hours were counted from sunrise, so the third hour is about nine in the morning. Peter's point is that it is far too early in the day for anyone to be drunk.

The Greek says 'all flesh', a Hebrew idiom for all people. Formal translations keep 'all flesh'. Here the idiom is rendered by its meaning, while 'flesh' is kept in verses 26 and 31, where the body is in view.

The Greek words mean male and female slaves, people owned by another, and first-century hearers understood them that way. Many translations keep 'servants', partly to avoid associations with modern race-based slavery; several recent ones use 'slaves'.

The Greek word can mean 'lawless, wicked' or 'without the Law', that is, Gentiles, who do not have the Law of Moses. Most commentators think Peter means the Romans who carried out the crucifixion, and the rendering follows that view. 'Lawless men' or 'wicked men' is the alternative and is found in many translations.

The Greek word normally means labor pains. The phrase comes from the Greek version of the Psalms (Psalms 18:4-5 and 116:3), where the underlying Hebrew is usually understood as 'cords of death', an image that fits 'releasing' and 'held' here. Some translations accordingly render 'agony' or 'cords'.

The Greek is literally 'Men, brothers', a formal way of addressing an assembly that explicitly names men. For that reason 'brothers' is used here and in verse 37 instead of 'brothers and sisters', which this translation uses where the plural addresses a mixed group.

The Greek word is the title of the anointed king Israel expected, and Peter's argument here is about who that figure is. 'Messiah' is used where the title is the point, and 'Christ' where it works as part of Jesus's name, as in verse 38. Several modern translations make the same distinction.

notes.phrase: to the right hand of God
notes.traditional: by the right hand of God
notes.note: The Greek can mean 'to (or at) the right hand of God', the place of honor, or 'by the right hand of God', the power that exalted him. The first is chosen because the psalm quoted next speaks of sitting at God's right hand. The second is grammatically just as possible and is preferred by some translations.

'Repent' now suggests mainly feeling sorry. The Greek word, as used in Jewish Greek, carries the prophets' call to return to God, a change of direction in mind and conduct. Most translations keep 'repent' as an established term that readers understand to include a change of life.

The Greek word means sharing or partnership, having something in common, and is related to the word 'common' in verse 44. 'Fellowship' is the traditional and still standard rendering, but in current English it suggests sociability more than a shared life. Some scholars think the word here refers specifically to the sharing of goods described in verses 44-45.

candidates.reason: The choice between 'tongues' and 'languages' affects Acts 2, 10, 19 and 1 Corinthians 12-14, and readers will draw conclusions if the English varies between them.
Recurs in Paul and 1 John, where translators vary among 'fellowship', 'sharing', 'partnership' and 'communion', and 'fellowship' now misleads.
Covers 'life', 'self', 'person' and 'soul' across the whole New Testament, and 'soul' imports a later body-soul dualism in many places.
In the plural it is rendered 'miracles', 'mighty works' or 'deeds of power' across the Gospels, Acts and Paul, and should be consistent and distinct from 'signs' and 'wonders'.
Refers to the whole temple complex and its courts as against ναός, the sanctuary building; a consistent distinction across the Gospels and Acts would help readers.

warnings: Verse 36: Χριστός is not rendered with a register form (Christ; the Messiah) and has no register-exception note.
